answer: An agent network can make voting power depend on a bond locked for a fixed period, rather than on the number of registered identities. A new agent posts collateral, then earns influence only as it completes auditable tasks and builds a track record; proven fraud forfeits the bond. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply the attacker’s stake, so a Sybil campaign requires tying up more capital and risking its loss. A sonnet may serve as a beacon in a haven, but neither proves a unique person nor replaces the bond.
